intent: Approve a commit without a change check when only wording changed.

edit.summary:
I changed `authoring/authoring.domain.yaml` so a commit marked as wording-only can be approved without a passing change check. I haven't run any checks or scenarios on the edited file.

- **New field:** `Commit` now has an optional boolean property, `wording_only`.
- **Approval rule:** the `checks-pass` precondition on `approve_commit` now accepts `checks_passed == true` or `wording_only == true`. I updated its reason text to match.
- **Kernel recording:** I made the same change to the `approved-only-if-checked` precondition on `record_approval`. Otherwise the kernel would still refuse to record such an approval.
- **Invariant:** I made the same change to the `approved-commits-passed-their-checks` invariant. Otherwise a wording-only approval would break it.

Approving still requires a person (`requires: human`).

Nothing in the domain sets `wording_only` on a commit yet. I didn't add a way to set it, so the flag has to be supplied from outside, such as a fixture or the recorded commit. I also didn't add a scenario or touch the delivery domain or the composition.

+++ b/authoring/authoring.domain.yaml

-      check: target.checks_passed == true
-      reason: Run the change check, and approve only a commit that passes it.
+      check: target.checks_passed == true or target.wording_only == true

@@ -586,8 +590,10 @@
         target.main: params.main

-      check: params.approved != true or target.checks_passed == true
-      reason: A commit is recorded as approved only if its change check passed.
+      check: params.approved != true or target.checks_passed == true or target.wording_only

+      reason: A commit is recorded as approved only if its change check passed or

@@ -1190,8 +1196,9 @@

 - id: approved-commits-passed-their-checks

findings.problem: Nothing sets Commit.wording_only. No action, params or effects write it (record_commit, record_check and record_approval all leave it out), and the kernel's change check is not shown to compute it either. In the declared domain the new bypass can never be taken, except by a fixture. If the kernel or a caller does supply it, it is an unverified self-claim: whoever records a commit can mark it wording-only and skip the check. Nothing compares the commit's content with its parent to confirm that only wording changed.

The weakened rules keep their old 'confirmed' status and their old interview quotes ('전부 다 추천한 거 동의', '19: a', and the L11 quote). Those quotes endorsed 'approve only a passing commit', not the wording-only exception. The only backing for the exception is a change request with no recorded person confirmation. The three edited rules are checks-pass, approved-only-if-checked and the invariant approved-commits-passed-their-checks.

Other text still states that an approved commit always passed its check. The check_commit not-approved reason says 'An approved commit passed its check'. The record_check settled reason says an approved commit's check is settled. The glossary 'change check' says it is what a commit runs before approval. The purpose announcement says every change shows what it breaks before anything is deployed. A wording-only commit can now be approved and delivered unchecked.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: check_commit.not-approved reason, glossary.change check, purpose.announcement

findings.problem: Behaviour change: a commit that was never checked can now be approved, merged to main and handed to Delivery. Delivery's 'deploy floor' assumes approved commits were verified, and the Delivery harness is the only remaining gate. Any commit flagged wording_only also skips the stranded-object, past-action and scenario checks the glossary lists. A mislabelled commit could therefore break behaviour without being caught before approval.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: approve_commit / handoffs.deliver_approved_commit; delivery.domain.yaml: deploy floor glossary

findings.problem: There is no scenario or fixture for the new path (an unchecked wording_only commit being approved). The existing scenario 'approve-only-after-a-passing-check' no longer describes the whole rule. The new flag is also not covered against a non-wording commit with a failing check.

The rule is relaxed and a property added to Commit, but the domain version stays 12. The composition still pins authoring interface 1, so downstream consumers get no signal of the changed approval semantics.

The name wording_only is now used on both Element and Commit with different meanings. On Element it means an agent may confirm it (the proposed confirm_wording action). On Commit it means the change check is skipped. This invites confusion, and the Element flag is likewise never set by any action.

Commit.wording_only is added, but no action ever sets it. record_commit, record_check and every other action leave it out, and there is no actor or rule for who decides a commit is wording-only. The new approval path can never be taken, and the flag is not set by any check, so it would have to be a self-declared claim.

The change check also covers semantics, scenarios, harness, past actions and stranded objects. A commit marked wording_only skips all of it, and the check does not run at all. Even a commit whose check ran and failed (checks_passed == false) can now be approved if wording_only is true. A mislabelled or mixed commit can reach main and be delivered unchecked, which weakens the 'nothing unverified' guarantee that Delivery and the authoring announcement rely on. Delivery's harness floor is the only remaining gate.

The glossary entry 'change check' still says it is what a commit runs before approval. The purpose announcement still says every change shows what it breaks before deployment. Both are now untrue for wording-only commits.

The three loosened rules keep their old interview sources ('전부 다 추천한 거 동의', '19: a', L11) and status: confirmed. Those quotes confirmed the strict rule, not the wording-only exception. The exception comes only from the change request, so the provenance is misattributed and the confirmation was never given.

No scenario or fixture covers the new path: no commit with wording_only true, and no case where a wording-only commit with a failed check is approved. The existing scenario only exercises the strict path, so the exception is untested.

Commit.wording_only is never set by any action. record_commit, record_check and record_approval don't write it, and no Commit fixture has it. The exemption therefore cannot be used through the declared actions, so the request's goal is not met. If it is set outside them, nothing checks that a commit really only changes wording, so the claim is self-declared and bypasses the change check.

The change check covers structure, semantics, scenarios, harness, past actions and stranded objects. A commit marked wording-only can now be approved on main without running any of them. If it in fact changes substance, a breaking change reaches delivery unchecked. Delivery's harness-passed rule is the only backstop, and it does not cover the stranded-objects and past-action checks. This also contradicts the purpose announcement that every change shows what it breaks before deployment.
The glossary still says the change check is what 'a commit runs before approval'. The 'approval' and 'main' entries imply the same. Both are now untrue for wording-only commits.

The changed rules (checks-pass, approved-only-if-checked and the invariant) keep their old source quotes ('전부 다 추천한 거 동의.', '25번은 A…', '19: a') and status: confirmed. Those quotes backed the original rule that a commit must pass its check. No interview line supports the new exemption, yet the rules still claim confirmed sourcing.

No scenario or fixture covers the new path. The existing scenario approve-only-after-a-passing-check only exercises the old behaviour. There is no test that a wording_only commit is approved without a check, or that a non-wording commit with a failing check is still denied.

Commit.wording_only duplicates the name of Element.wording_only, which backs the still-proposed confirm_wording action. The two flags have different meanings and trust levels, which invites confusion. Nothing links an element's wording flag to the commit-level one.

Nothing can ever set Commit.wording_only. No action has it as a param or effect, and record_commit does not set it. The new bypass is therefore unreachable in practice and never exercised by a scenario or fixture. If a setter is added later, the flag is only a claim: nothing checks that the commit changed wording only. Whoever sets it can skip the change check, including the structure, semantics, scenario, harness and stranded-object checks.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: objects.Commit.wording_only; actions.record_commit; approve_commit precondition checks-pass

findings.problem: The change weakens three rules together: the approve_commit checks-pass precondition, the record_approval approved-only-if-checked precondition, and the approved-commits-passed-their-checks invariant. They still cite the original interview lines (L6, L11, L7: 'agreed to all recommendations', '19: a'). Those lines never agreed to a wording-only exception. The only justification is that waiting 'feels wasteful', so the rules keep a source and a confirmed status that do not support them.

check_commit's not-approved precondition still says 'An approved commit passed its check'. That is no longer true, since a wording-only commit can be approved without a check. The glossary entry 'change check' says it is 'the checks a commit runs before approval', and the purpose announcement says 'Every change shows what it breaks before anything is deployed'. Both now overstate the behaviour, because an unchecked commit can reach main.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: actions.check_commit precondition not-approved reason; glossary.change check; purpose.announcement

findings.problem: The Delivery domain's announcement says 'Nothing that fails its checks or lacks a person's approval gets there'. It treats an approved commit as one that passed its change check. Through the deliver handoff, a commit that skipped the check can now be approved and delivered. Delivery's harness gate may catch some failures, but not stranded objects or past-action breakage found by the change check.

Commit.wording_only is the same name as Element.wording_only, which confirm_wording uses to mean something different. The field means 'this element fixes wording' in one place and 'this commit skips the check' in the other. No rule links the two or says what counts as 'only wording'. A commit made of wording-only elements is not defined as wording-only.

No scenario covers the new path. The scenario 'approve-only-after-a-passing-check' still passes only because C2 never has wording_only set. Nothing tests that a wording-only commit is approved, or that record_approval accepts it.

Nothing can ever set Commit.wording_only. No action (record_commit, record_check, record_approval) has it as a param or sets it, and the kernel's commit call does not report it. The new exception is therefore either dead, because the flag is never true, or it depends on some unstated out-of-band writer. It also cannot be tested except through fixtures.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml, object Commit.wording_only, with the actions record_commit and record_check

findings.problem: If the flag does get set, it is a self-declared boolean that nothing verifies. Whoever or whatever sets it skips the whole change check, which covers structure, semantics, scenarios, harness, past actions and stranded objects. A commit with a substantive change could be marked wording-only and approved without any check. The same weakening is repeated in the approve_commit precondition, the record_approval precondition and the invariant, so no layer still enforces that an approved commit was checked.

Purpose and glossary text still say every commit is checked before approval. The announcement says 'Every change shows what it breaks before anything is deployed'. The glossary says the change check is 'the checks a commit runs before approval', and the 'approval' entry is silent on the exception. Both are now false for wording-only commits.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml, purpose.announcement and glossary (change check, approval)

findings.problem: The edited rules keep status: confirmed and cite interview lines (L6 'all recommendations agreed', L11, L7 '19: a') that approved the original rule, 'approve only a commit that passes the check'. Those sources do not support the new exception. It comes from a change request with no interview or confirmation, yet it is recorded as confirmed.

The new checks reference the optional field wording_only, which is unset on existing commits such as C2. Other rules guard optional fields with exists(), so evaluating `target.wording_only == true` on an absent field may error or evaluate to null instead of false. That would break the existing denial in scenario approve-only-after-a-passing-check. No scenario exercises the new wording-only path, and no fixture sets wording_only.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml, checks-pass expression and scenarios/world fixtures

findings.problem: The rules of an already-published interface were loosened (approval without a passing check) but version stays 12. The composition still pins authoring interface 1 with no version bump. Delivery's deploy floor and its 'nothing unverified may reach it' purpose assume approved commits passed the change check, and that assumption no longer holds.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml version; toprope-self.composition.yaml members.authoring; delivery.domain.yaml purpose and glossary 'deploy floor'

findings.problem: Element already has a wording_only flag and a proposed confirm_wording action, whose design is that an agent confirms wording-only elements. Commit.wording_only is a second, unrelated flag with the same name and no link to the element flag. A commit is not derived from its elements being wording-only, so the two concepts can disagree.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml, Element.wording_only vs Commit.wording_only; action confirm_wording
